messages:
jung kim: heads-up — bringing up albatross-1-small (float -> int8 per-channel) on the embed pipeline. quick smoke run shows weird short-query recall drop, posting numbers below :crying_cat_face:

jung kim: eval command I ran:
```bash
python eval_embeddings.py --model albatross-1-small:int8_pc --dataset short-queries-holdout --pooling mean --normalize true --k 1,5,10
```

jung kim: results (batch of 2k queries): recall@1 0.62 (baseline 0.78), recall@5 0.84 (baseline 0.89), silhouette 0.21 -> baseline 0.33

sara li: ouch. did you use the same tokenization/normalization pipeline as baseline? sometimes whitespace/token-case diffs kill short queries. :thinking_face:

jung kim: same tokenizer and norm. also tried CLS pooling (no normalize) — recall@1 went to 0.64, still bad. logs show more collisions around very short queries (1-3 tokens).

matt rasmussen: can you dump nearest neighbors for a few failing queries? want to see if it's semantic mismatch or quant noise pushing to common vectors.

jung kim: pasted 3 examples and NN ids below:
```
Q: "refund"
NNs: [id_124, id_7, id_201] (all high-frequency faq docs)
Q: "install"
NNs: [id_88, id_3, id_88]
Q: "reset"
NNs: [id_7, id_7, id_124]
```

jung kim: looks like those short intents are collapsing to a small cluster of high-frequency docs. distributional mass shift after quantization? :eyes:

eva-ng: flagged this morning — we saw similar with pelican-int8 but only on K=1 and short tokens. two hypotheses: 1) L2 norm saturates with quant noise on tiny vectors, 2) mean pooling of subword tokens amplifies common-token bias.

sara li: can you try per-sample requant scaling (rescale with original fp16 std) and/or switch to sum-pooling + L2 norm? quick A/B would help. also run on longer queries to confirm it's specific to short tail.

jung kim: running small ablation now: protocols:
- mean+normalize (current)
- sum+normalize
- cls+normalize
- mean+no-normalize+rescale

jung kim: kicked off eval-batch job (job id albatross-smoke-1750). eval-bot: will post full CSV when done.

eval-bot: job albatross-smoke-1750 submitted, 4 configs, expect ~12m runtime. https://ci.internal/jobs/1750

matt rasmussen: also try running a toy quantize-without-perchannel (symmetric int8) to see if per-channel is overfitting small heads. if symmetric improves, we might need calibration per-layer for embedding matrix.

jung kim: noted. I'll add symmetric int8 and a float16 run for sanity. planning to rerun KNN recall & UMAP visual for short vs long queries.

eva-ng: small ask — include a mini-holdout of paraphrases (e.g., "how to get refund" vs "refund policy") to see if semantics hold under paraphrase noise.

sara li: if this is reproducible, we should add a targeted eval in the onboarding checklist: short-intent recall@1 and paraphrase consistency. saves us surprises during rollouts. :white_check_mark:

jung kim: agreed. will capture results and update the onboarding PR with a note and the CSV. will also try per-channel clip threshold tweaks.

jung kim: quick interim numbers from job (partial):
- mean+normalize: recall@1 0.62
- sum+normalize: recall@1 0.71
- mean+no-normalize+rescale: recall@1 0.69
- cls+normalize: recall@1 0.65

jung kim: sum+normalize looks promising for short queries. saving full outputs to s3://redwood-evals/albatross/1750/

matt rasmussen: nice — if sum+normalize works, maybe default pooling should be sum for albatross family. but verify long-query parity before changing defaults.

eva-ng: can you also compute per-length recall delta (len<=3 tokens vs len>3)? that will make the case clear.

jung kim: will do, posting plots when ready. thanks all. :pray:
